title: Write newline-delimited JSON. The MCP stdio transport does not use `Content-Length` frames.
body:
**🗄️ Data Integrity & Integration** | ** Critical** | **⚡ Quick win** **Write newline-delimited JSON. The MCP stdio transport does not use `Content-Length` frames.** The MCP stdio transport (spec 2024-11-05, the version this server advertises at Line 157) delimits each message with `\n`. It has no LSP-style headers. Cursor, Claude Code and the official SDKs split stdout on newlines and `JSON.parse`/validate each line. With this output: - The first line is `Content-Length: N\r`, which is not JSON. - Each body has no trailing newline, so it is glued to the next frame's header. Every response after `initialize` is unparseable. The advertised integration therefore cannot work. This matches the learning that non-JSON-RPC output on stdout breaks stdio clients. Write the compact JSON followed by `'\n'`. If Content-Length input must stay supported, record the framing of the incoming message and use that framing only for the reply.
🐛 Proposed fix
```diff --- "a/src/mcp/McpServer.cpp" +++ "b/src/mcp/McpServer.cpp" @@ -111,13 +111,12 @@ } } void McpServer::writeMessage(const QJsonObject &msg) { - const QByteArray body = QJsonDocument(msg).toJson(QJsonDocument::Compact); - const QByteArray frame = "Content-Length: " + QByteArray::number(body.size()) + "\r\n\r\n" + body; + const QByteArray frame = QJsonDocument(msg).toJson(QJsonDocument::Compact) + '\n'; fwrite(frame.constData(), 1, static_cast(frame.size()), stdout); fflush(stdout); } void McpServer::handleMessage(const QJsonObject &msg) { ```
Based on learnings: "any non-JSON-RPC output … written to stdout before or between JSON-RPC messages breaks clients like Python MCP SDK's stdio_client".

Review comment at @src/mcp/McpServer.cpp around lines 114 - 120: Update McpServer::writeMessage to write each compact JSON message followed by a newline, removing the Content-Length header framing so stdio clients can parse each response as one JSON line. After applying the fix, consider running `coderabbit review --agent` for local review. Visit https://docs.coderabbit.ai/cli?utm_source=ghpr ```

title: The foreign round-trip comparison ignores the block of each revision and its `payload`.
body:
`283-290`: **🎯 Functional Correctness** | ** Minor** | **⚡ Quick win** **The foreign round-trip comparison ignores the block of each revision and its `payload`.** `compare_revision_lists` compares only `kind`, `author`, `start`, `end` and `text`. Line 288 drops `payload`, even though `norm` computes it. The block is never part of the comparison. Suppose the exporter or importer attaches a revision to the wrong paragraph with the same offsets. The `--foreign` check still prints "round-trip OK". That is the round-trip data loss this script should catch. `scripts/qa-interop.py` (`norm`, lines 128-142) already compares a block index. Fetch the body together with the revisions. Map `block_id` to its body index on both sides, then compare that index and `payload`.

```diff -def compare_revision_lists(got: list[dict], want: list[dict]) -> None: - def norm(r: dict) -> dict: +def compare_revision_lists(got: list[dict], got_body: list, want: list[dict], want_body: list) -> None: + def index_of(body: list) -> dict: + return {b.get("id"): i for i, b in enumerate(body)} + + def norm(r: dict, idx: dict) -> dict: return { "kind": r.get("kind"), + "block": idx.get(r.get("block_id"), -1), "author": r.get("author"), @@ - for key in ("kind", "author", "start", "end", "text"): + for key in ("kind", "block", "author", "start", "end", "text", "payload"): ``` In `foreign_roundtrip`, add `{"tool": "document_get", "args": {}}` to the reimport playbook. title: Assign missing block ids after the whole body loads. The current order can create duplicate ids.
body:
`1292-1297`: **🗄️ Data Integrity & Integration** | ** Minor** | **⚡ Quick win** **Assign missing block ids after the whole body loads. The current order can create duplicate ids.** `assignId` calls `nextCounter`, and `nextCounter` scans only the blocks already pushed. Example input: `body: [{"type":"paragraph"}, {"id":"p1"}]`. The first block gets `p1`, then the second block keeps its explicit `p1`. `findBlock` and `indexOf` then return the first match. An edit, comment, xref, or revision that targets `p1` then applies to the wrong block. This load path accepts hostile or hand-written JSON.
🐛 Proposed fix
```diff - for (const auto &b : o.value(QStringLiteral("body")).toArray()) { - Block blk = Block::fromJson(b.toObject()); - if (blk.id.isEmpty()) - d.assignId(blk); - d.body.push_back(blk); - } + for (const auto &b : o.value(QStringLiteral("body")).toArray()) + d.body.push_back(Block::fromJson(b.toObject())); + QSet seen; + for (Block &blk : d.body) { + if (blk.id.isEmpty() || seen.contains(blk.id)) + d.assignId(blk); + seen.insert(blk.id); + } ```

title: Quote and sanitize field arguments before they go into `\fldinst`.
body:
`255-267`: **🔒 Security & Privacy** | ** Minor** | **⚡ Quick win** **Quote and sanitize field arguments before they go into `\fldinst`.** `r.fieldArg` and `r.link` are interpolated raw into `MERGEFIELD`, `DOCVARIABLE`, `FILLIN "…"` and `HYPERLINK "…"`. Any remaining text is then parsed as field switches, for example `\l`, `\o` or `\*`. If a `MERGEFIELD` or `DOCVARIABLE` name contains a space, the reader splits it into a name and switches. Word and the native reader then receive a different field from the one stored in the document. Escape `"` as `\"` inside the quoted arguments. Quote the names of `MERGEFIELD` and `DOCVARIABLE` fields. Also applies to: 288-291

Do not assign `root.value` inside `bump`. The assignment breaks the caller's binding.
body:
`14-20`: **🎯 Functional Correctness** | ** Minor** | **⚡ Quick win** **Do not assign `root.value` inside `bump`. The assignment breaks the caller's binding.** Callers bind `value` to controller state, for example `value: app.pageColumns` and `value: Math.round(app.marginsMm[...])` in Sidebar.qml. The first wheel or click assigns `root.value = next`, which permanently removes that binding. After undo, opening another document or switching tabs, the spin box shows a stale value. Emit the proposed value and let the owner update the bound state. ```diff - signal valueModified() + signal valueModified(int value) ... - root.value = next - root.valueModified() + root.valueModified(next) ``` The existing call sites keep working because they read `value` inside the handler.

title: Use a per-user socket name and restrict socket access.
body:
`14-24`: **🔒 Security & Privacy** | ** Minor** | **⚡ Quick win** **Use a per-user socket name and restrict socket access.** If `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` is unset, the socket path is a fixed `/tmp/aioffice.sock`. Examples are SSH sessions without `pam_systemd`, containers and some CI hosts. Another local user can create that path first. The sticky bit on `/tmp` then makes `removeServer` fail, `listen` fails, and `AppController` ignores the `false` return. `aioffice call` and `aioffice mcp` then send document content and tool arguments to the other user's process and accept forged results. Line 100 has a related problem: it also removes the socket of a second running instance without checking it. Add the user ID to the path, for example `aioffice-.sock`. Call `server->setSocketOptions(QLocalServer::UserAccessOption)`. Before `removeServer`, check whether a live server answers on the path. Also applies to: 99-102
